messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall: High latency detected for /generate endpoints in eu-west-1. p95 spiked to 650ms, p99 ~2.8s over the last 5m. Potential preproc/tokenizer hotspot. Automated mitigation hasn't triggered yet. Please ack. :rotating_light:
oncall: acked — I'm on it. grabbing traces now, assigning to sam k and mika j.
sam k: seeing a lot of long preproc durations from preproc-v2 pods (cpu high, syscalls up). Top_span: prompt_builder:template_expand (avg 320ms, p99 2.2s).
mika j: logs show JSON mode expansion for a few requests where tool schemas are large (~40kb). The prompt template renderer is repeatedly re-parsing tool schemas per request.
lee: looks like cache misses on template-cache. eviction rate jumped when we had a short burst of long user prompts at 16:03 UTC.
taylor r: streaming stalls reported downstream in the streaming_proxy: many connections idle while preproc spins. correlates with p99 tokenization timeouts. Trace: https://console.redwood/trace/trace-id/8b7f1e
sam k: reproduction: send a request with `tool_schema` containing big enum arrays and `json_mode: true`. preproc CPU climbs to 95% and latency cascades. snippet of problematic payload: ```{"tools": [{"name": "lookup","schema": {"type":"object","properties": {"options": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":500}}}}]}```
oncall: initial customer impact: 3 customers on EU hosted cluster reported soft failures (streaming stalls, partial responses). No full data loss but degraded SLOs. I'm marking severity P1 for latency SLO breach.
support-bot: Identified customers: acme-inc, bluewave, docs.ai — streaming sessions with partial/late tokens. Support notified via banner template; tickets created.
eng-sre: temporary mitigation options: 1) disable `json_mode` for incoming requests at the routing layer for eu-west-1, 2) enable template-cache read-through with TTL bump, 3) scale preproc-v2 to +3 pods.
mika j: preference is 1+3 short term. Disabling json_mode per-route is fast (flip a flag in routing config), scaling takes ~60s. Need approval to patch live config.
aria: oncall, do we have rollback if disabling json_mode causes app regressions? Some customers rely on JSON mode.
oncall: we'll do a scoped rule: disable json_mode for requests where `tool_schema.size > 10kb` and route everything else normally. That should minimize customer regressions.
taylor r: I can push the scoped rule now. Command: ```ytt -f routing/overrides.yaml -v region=eu-west-1 -v block_json_schema_threshold=10240 | kubectl apply -f -```
sam k: also create a short-term patch in preproc to add early-return for enormous schema sizes (reject with 400 + diagnostic). We'll feature-flag it.
lee: I'm increasing template-cache size on preproc-v2 and pinning eviction to LRU-heavy items. Applying config now.
eng-sre: scaling preproc-v2 by +3 pods (kubectl scale deployment preproc-v2 --replicas=7) — started at 16:12 UTC.
mika j: after flips at 16:14 UTC the p95 dropped to 180ms within 2 minutes, p99 down to ~650ms and streaming stalls disappeared from active error logs.
oncall: Customer update: posted interim status to affected customers, asked for retries. Support will follow up in 30m.
support-bot: tickets updated: https://support.redwood/INC-10987, INC-10988, INC-10989.
sam k: root cause hypothesis: prompt template renderer doesn't memoize parsed tool schemas in JSON mode; combined with template interpolation and large enums causes O(N^2) parse/validate cycles per token for some templates.
taylor r: postmortem action items being created: - add memoization in renderer, - add schema-size enforcement/validation at ingress, - telemetry for template-cache hit rate, - per-route json_mode opt-out config.
oncall: handing to eng-sre for follow-up and postmortem. Closing live mitigation loop — watch metrics for next 2 hours. If p99 > 1s reopen. :white_check_mark:
eng-sre: noted. Collecting flame graphs and allocation traces and will open a high-priority PR for renderer memoization. Link to traces + logs: https://console.redwood/logs?query=preproc-v2+%22template_expand%22
aria: thanks all. incident thread will remain open until postmortem published. If anyone sees regression ping here. :coffee:
